amendments.rule: Substantivize with no English determiner: `τὰ` → *things*, `τοῦ` → *of him who*, `τοὺς` → *we who*, `τῷ` → *that which*. Head such a unit on the nominal word, not on the relativizer. The English expression may bring its own determiner — `τὰ` → *the things*, `τὸ` → *the part*, `οἱ` → *the one* and *the other* — and the head is still the nominal word and never the determiner. Rule 17's *on the* → *the* is the contrast: there the article's own case is what the preposition realizes, so nothing nominal competes with *the*. Where a participle follows, rule 32 splits this instead and the article keeps only the pronoun — where the ASV writes one. Where the ASV writes for such an article a determiner and a **supplied nominal** in place of a pronoun, rules 102 and 103 give the article both words, headed on the nominal, and the participle keeps the relativizer, any supplied copula and its own verb: `τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην` → *even the wisdom that hath been hidden* gives *the wisdom* to the article and *that hath been hidden* to the participle. Rule 32's *and nothing else* limits what the article may absorb beyond the English the ASV wrote for it, as rule 90 already reads that phrase, and it does not deny it a nominal where no pronoun was written. Rule 103's article clause is what folds that nominal rather than marking it `added`, and it folds it however plainly the nominal echoes a noun the same verse expresses elsewhere, no noun being expressed inside the article's own phrase; GAL.3.20 is the contrast, its article governing an expressed noun so that the article's phrase is already complete and the repeat stands in a slot no token governs. A supplied appositional *even* standing in front of such a phrase is untouched by this and remains its own `added` unit under rule 105, realizing no part of the article.
amendments.why: Rule 22's closing sentence and rule 32 both say without qualification that where a participle follows, the article keeps only the pronoun. 1CO.2.7 is the case they did not consider: the ASV wrote no pronoun for τήν but a determiner and a supplied nominal, *the wisdom*, in front of the participle. Read as it stood, rule 22 sends a later pass to a bare *the* on the article and an `added` *wisdom* — the reading rule 103's article clause forbids in terms, since no noun is expressed inside that article's phrase. Rules 102 and 103 already decide the case (102 recording all fifty-three units of an article taking a determiner plus a nominal as headed on the nominal, 103 folding such a nominal however plainly it echoes a noun the verse expresses elsewhere), so this is a narrowing of an over-broad sentence rather than a new judgment, and it is returned as an amendment so the sentence itself is corrected instead of leaving a cross-reference for whoever reads rule 22 first. The final sentence is added so the amendment cannot be read as pulling 1CO.2.7's *even* out of rule 105's article-carrier arm.

conventions: A substantival article governing a bare adjective, where the ASV recasts the phrase as a finite relative clause, splits exactly as rule 32 splits a participle: the article takes the antecedent pronoun and the adjective keeps the relativizer, the supplied copula and its own word. τοῖς τελείοις → *them* / *that are fullgrown* at 2:6 and ὁ … πνευματικός → *he* / *that is spiritual* at 2:15. Rules 20 and 32 record the articular adjective only in apposition to an expressed pronoun, which empties the article; where no such pronoun stands the article is what supplies it.

A bare conditional εἰ is its own `unrepresented` unit where the ASV marks the protasis by inversion and writes no *if*: 2:8 εἰ … ἔγνωσαν → *had they known it* leaves the particle empty, the fronted *had* being the verb's own pluperfect auxiliary under rule 9, as the same verse's ἔγνωκεν → *hath known* keeps its own. Rule 50's *had* belongs to ἄν only where ἄν stands, and here it stands in the apodosis and takes *would*. A reference comparison will report the particle as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

report: Checked all 29 candidate lemma groups, then read the 16 verse dumps end to end for the splits the table cannot see (added-vs-fold, head choice, supplied-word placement). No construction is analysed two ways without the source or the ASV's own wording licensing the difference, so patches is empty.

Determiner placement is uniform on rules 51/58: where a Greek article stands it takes the supplied determiner (2:11 τοῦ → *of a*; 2:6, 2:8, 2:11, 2:12, 2:14 → *of the*), and where the phrase is anarthrous the noun takes it (2:5 *the wisdom*, *the power*; 2:6 σοφίαν → *a wisdom*; 2:7 *a mystery*; 2:9 *the heart*; 2:13 *the Spirit*; 2:16 *the mind*), 2:14 Ψυχικὸς … ἄνθρωπος → *the … man* putting it on the noun across the adjective under rule 58. The article before θεοῦ/θεός is unrepresented in all six occurrences (2:1, 2:7, 2:9, 2:10, 2:12 twice, 2:14), the case *of* staying with the noun.

Supplied generic nominals are placed by carrier class and not by English adjacency: to the article where one governs the phrase (2:7 τήν → *the wisdom*; 2:11, 2:12, 2:14 τά → *the things*; 2:15 τά → *things* with πάντα bare, which is rule 17's own τὰ πάντα), and to the anarthrous word where none does (2:10 πάντα → *all things* head *all*; 2:13 πνευματικά → *spiritual things* and πνευματικοῖς → *with spiritual words*; 2:10 βάθη → *deep things* head *deep*, rule 66). The substantival article recast with a finite relative clause splits the same way in all three of its verses: 2:6 τοῖς → *them*, 2:9 τοῖς → *for them*, 2:15 ὁ → *he*.

The chapter carries exactly one `added` unit — the appositional *even* at 2:7, on rule 105's substantival-article arm — and every other supplied word folds onto a token whose English it completes. There is no fold-here/add-there split, which is the shape the candidate table is blind to.

The one place the contract genuinely misdirects is 2:7. Rules 22 and 32 say flatly that where a participle follows, the article keeps only the pronoun; here the ASV wrote no pronoun but a determiner and a supplied nominal (*the wisdom*), which rules 102 and 103 give the article. The verse pass reasoned that out in its own note; the amendment below writes it into rule 22 so the next pass does not have to, and does not disturb the `added` *even*.

BSB, four disagreements, none a genuine error. 2:6 τῶν: rule 31's second attributive article before a participle whose head noun ἀρχόντων is expressed — the relativizer *who* is the participle's helper. 2:11 καί: rule 100, unanimous across thirteen corpus units, οὕτως taking *even so* whole and no *also* written. 2:13 ἐν: the ASV writes no second *in*, and rule 36 leaves a preposition empty only where English realizes it nowhere — 2:3 writes all three *in*s out and aligns each, so the difference is the ASV's. 2:8 εἰ: the ASV marks the protasis by inversion and writes no *if*; the fronted *had* is the verb's own pluperfect auxiliary under rule 9, as the same verse's ἔγνωκεν → *hath known* keeps its own, and ἄν takes the apodosis *would* under rule 50. The competing reading is already in the verse note; I did not change an accepted edge to move the rate.

Checked and rejected as non-splits: πρός *unto*/*with* (2:1, 2:3), δέ and καί rendered various ways, ἐν *in*/*among*, εἰ μή → *save* as noncompositional at 2:2 and 2:11 twice against the bare conditional at 2:8, and the copula going to the predicate at 2:4, 2:6, 2:11, 2:12, 2:15 under rule 53 against the expressed copula at 2:14.
